assessments.reasoning: The Autoconf mirror serves config/elisp-comp at commit 99a48ad6c1e3f446717e1f8fec2fb1ae76b09f2e. Its FSF copyright header identifies the Free Software Foundation, Inc. The receipt’s 2,094-byte file digest matches the claim revision. Bytes [129,1087) cover the GPL notice and the complete operative exception.

The License Index’s own SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 admits historical editions and defines an exception as an additional permission or documented modification, with affected editions supported separately. Bytes [640,783) supply the taxonomy criterion. The index owns the editorial mapping.

challenge.method: Following SCES-1.0 §§2–4 and protocol stage 7, I reopened the exact materials, checked each dependency for authority, integrity and scope, and tested the proposed identity against the standalone Configure Script Exception and the section 7 form. I traced the pronouns in the notice and checked the script’s stated purpose.
challenge.results: elisp-comp byte-compiles Emacs Lisp files. The generated configuration script is something the containing program must have. The permission governs distribution of elisp-comp itself. Its exception paragraph ends at “the rest of that program.” The section 7 sentence that distinguishes the GNU Config specimen is absent.

limitations: Historical is the index’s editorial state. The source attests the notice in this specimen. Other files and present-day publisher practice require separate evidence.

Across this review, the Autoconf 2.59 and GCC 14.2.0 edition labels use the supplied specimen-to-revision bindings. The connector returned immutable source commits and matching file digests. Separate publisher release-tag objects were available only for the SPDX release.

The three policy documents were read at commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710. The adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce is the supplied pin. This review did not independently reconstruct the adoption bundle or assess release qualification.
reasoning: The GNU Autoconf specimen says “you may include it” and identifies the object as “this file,” elisp-comp. The permission applies when the distributor includes that file in a program containing an Autoconf-generated configuration script. The permitted terms are those used for the rest of that program. This supports the generic exception identity and its historical registry mapping.
